filename: Deep learning to represent sub-grid processes in climate models.pdf
title: Deep learning to represent sub-grid processes in climate models
parameterization_target: atmospheric sub-grid convective and radiative tendencies of temperature and moisture, surface precipitation, and radiative fluxes at TOA and surface
code_availability: https://gitlab.com/mspritch/spcam3.0-neural-net (branch: nn fbp engy ess) and https://github.com/raspstephan/CBRAIN-CAM
testbed_rationale: Seminal study coupling deep learning sub-grid parameterization into a global GCM (CBRAIN-CAM) trained on multi-scale CRM data; codebase and methodology form a standard testbed for ML parameterization research.
pain_points: Poor generalization/extrapolation to out-of-sample climate regimes (e.g., temperatures exceeding the training distribution by 4K)
Reduced variability and overly smooth sub-grid heating/moistening tendencies in the boundary layer due to deterministic MSE minimization on chaotic targets
Omission of condensed water species prevents exact moisture conservation
Instabilities and unphysical artifacts when using shallow neural network architectures in prognostic mode
Inability to tune the parameterization once deployed online without parallel coupled retraining
extraction_notes: The preprint document is arXiv:1806.04731v3, later published in PNAS (2018). Input vector size is 94 and output vector size is 65 across 30 vertical levels.
